description: Created by Ludovic in Yaounde for collaborative work on the selected NASA challenge. Open to a friend and future teammates interested in architecture, design, research, and technical skills.
summary: Terra Trace turns 25 years of NASA Earth observations into a story anyone can follow. It starts with the whole planet, zooms into the Congo Basin, and ends in Yaoundé, Cameroon, our most detailed case. We ran robust trend tests (Mann-Kendall, Seasonal Mann-Kendall, Hamed-Rao correction, Sen's slope with confidence intervals, Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate) on NASA POWER, MERRA-2 and CERES series for 2001-2025. Result for Yaoundé: afternoon maximum temperature rises about +0.78 °C per decade and relative humidity drops about 1.6 points per decade (both robust); the apparent rainfall decline is not statistically proven, and we say so. A 'For you' section translates each trend into what it means for an ordinary person (student, farmer, parent, city planner), with simple, intermediate and advanced levels; advanced science stays optional. A globe, live NASA POWER data, and 'Ask Terra', an AI assistant grounded only in our results and NASA data, let anyone explore and ask questions. Every number shows its NASA source.
details:
Terra Trace turns 25 years of NASA Earth observations into a story anyone can follow. It starts with the whole planet, zooms into the Congo Basin, and ends in Yaoundé, Cameroon, our most detailed case. We ran robust trend tests (Mann-Kendall, Seasonal Mann-Kendall, Hamed-Rao correction, Sen's slope with confidence intervals, Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate) on NASA POWER, MERRA-2 and CERES series for 2001-2025. Result for Yaoundé: afternoon maximum temperature rises about +0.78 °C per decade and relative humidity drops about 1.6 points per decade (both robust); the apparent rainfall decline is not statistically proven, and we say so. A 'For you' section translates each trend into what it means for an ordinary person (student, farmer, parent, city planner), with simple, intermediate and advanced levels; advanced science stays optional. A globe, live NASA POWER data, and 'Ask Terra', an AI assistant grounded only in our results and NASA data, let anyone explore and ask questions. Every number shows its NASA source.

Live website: https://trend-detective-congo.vercel.app

Data sources: NASA POWER (https://power.larc.nasa.gov/), MERRA-2 (https://gmao.gsfc.nasa.gov/reanalysis/MERRA-2/), CERES (https://ceres.larc.nasa.gov/), HydroSHEDS (https://www.hydrosheds.org/), OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org/).

Use of AI: We used AI coding assistants to help write and test code, and Gemini powers the 'Ask Terra' chat, restricted to our computed results and NASA data. All statistics were computed by our own scripts; no numbers were generated by AI.
